Euler’s thirty-six officers need not all be entangled:
real AME(4,6)(4,6), families and classification

Palash Pandya Affiliation: Center for Theoretical Physics, Polish Academy of Sciences, Aleja Lotników 32/46, 02-668 Warsaw, Poland Affiliation: Center for Quantum-Enabled Computing, Center for Theoretical Physics, Polish Academy of Sciences, Aleja Lotników 32/46, 02-668 Warsaw, Poland
Abstract

Absolutely maximally entangled states of four six-level systems, AME(4,6)(4,6), are the quantum solutions of Euler’s problem of the thirty-six officers. Until recently all reported solutions were complex, and it was conjectured that no real orthogonal 2-unitary matrix of order 3636 exists. We give real AME(4,6)(4,6) states with 6060 non-zero coefficients in {±1,2}/72\{\pm 1,\sqrt{2}\}/\sqrt{72}. Of their thirty-six officers, 1212 are classical, as some must be whenever fewer than 7272 coefficients are non-zero. They lie in the −1-1 eigenspace of an order-44 local symmetry, and on their support the AME conditions become linear. We derive two closed-form families of AME(4,6)(4,6) states that meet at one of these states: a 1010-parameter family that is supported on 7272 basis states, and an 1111-parameter family on 6060 basis states. At each of its two ends the first family loses 1212 coefficients, and the AME states on the remaining 6060 basis states form an 1111-parameter family: the second family at one end, and an analogous family at the other. These two 6060-term families contain 40964096 real AME states up to diagonal local unitaries, 10241024 of which are limits of the first family. They fall into exactly 2020 classes under local unitaries and permutations of the parties, and we certify their separation with interval arithmetic.

I Introduction

A pure state of NN parties with dd levels each is absolutely maximally entangled, AME(N,d)(N,d), if every reduction to ⌊N/2⌋\lfloor N/2\rfloor parties is maximally mixed [1, 2]. Such states are perfect tensors. They underlie quantum secret sharing [1] and holographic codes [3], and 2-unitary matrices are dual-unitary gates of maximal entangling power [4, 5]. For four parties, writing U(i​j),(k​l)=d​ψi​j​k​lU_{(ij),(kl)}=d\,\psi_{ijkl}, the state is AME if and only if UU is 2-unitary: UU, its realignment URU^{R} and its partial transpose UΓU^{\Gamma} are all unitary [2]. Up to permutations of rows and columns, these three matrices are the reshapings of d​ψd\,\psi along the three bipartitions 12|3412|34, 13|2413|24 and 14|2314|23.

A pair of orthogonal Latin squares of order dd gives a 2-unitary permutation matrix, the classical case of the quantum combinatorial designs of Refs. [2, 6]. Such pairs exist for every d≥3d\geq 3 except d=6d=6 [7]: Euler’s problem of the 3636 officers has no solution [8, 9]. AME(4,2)(4,2) states do not exist at all [10]. An AME(4,6)(4,6) state, a quantum solution of Euler’s problem, was found by Rather et al. [11]. Further solutions include continuous families obtained from it [12], 2-unitary complex Hadamard matrices [13], constructions from biunimodular vectors [14] and hand-made solutions [15]. No pure stabilizer AME(4,6)(4,6) state exists [16, 17], and every quantum solution requires entanglement: mutually orthogonal quantum Latin squares of order six without entanglement do not exist [18].

All of these solutions are given with complex coefficients. In the Supplemental Material of Ref. [11] the authors write: “Further numerical results suggest that any 2-unitary matrix U36U_{36} has complex entries. Therefore, it is tempting to conjecture that there exists no solution in the set O⁡(36)O(36) of orthogonal matrices of this size.” A recent review lists the question as open problem (T2) [19]: “Is there an AME(4,6) state with real coefficients? Equivalently, is there an orthogonal 2-unitary matrix of order 36?” This question has now been answered in the affirmative, independently, by Bruzda [20], Rather [21], Hontarenko and Życzkowski [22], and the present work. With the permutation solutions for d≠2,6d\neq 2,6, it follows that a real AME(4,d)(4,d) state exists if and only if d≥3d\geq 3, exactly when a complex one does. We present the following results in this work. Section II presents our central result: an explicit real AME(4,6)(4,6) state with 6060 non-zero coefficients, the sparsest AME(4,6)(4,6) state we know of, whose 2-unitary representation consists of direct sums of 1×11\times 1 and 2×22\times 2 blocks. Of its 3636 officers, 1212 are classical, as some must be in any AME(4,6)(4,6) state with fewer than 7272 non-zero coefficients (Sec. VI). Section III describes its origin. It lies in the −1-1 eigenspace of the local symmetry u⊗4u^{\otimes 4}, u=diag⁡(i,−1,−1,−i,−i,−i)u=\mathrm{diag}(i,-1,-1,-i,-i,-i), and we show that the AME conditions are linear on its support. In Sec. IV two continuous families of AME(4,6)(4,6) states are presented in closed form, with supports on 7272 and 6060 basis states. The two families meet at the real state. In Sec. V we show that the families allow a complete classification of the real AME states with the two 6060-term supports at the ends of the 7272-term family: 40964096 states in exactly 2020 classes under local unitaries and party permutations, all of them isolated (numerically). All statements about our states are verified by self-contained scripts [23].

II A real AME(4,6)(4,6) state

If we index the basis states of each party as |i⟩\ket{i}, where i=0,…,5i=0,\dots,5, then we can write the state as an array of Euler’s officers where the first two parties carry rank aa and regiment bb, and the last two parties carry the state |ϕa​b⟩\ket{\phi_{ab}} attached to them:

|ψ⟩=172​∑a,b=05|a​b⟩⊗|ϕa​b⟩.\ket{\psi}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{72}}\sum_{a,b=0}^{5}\ket{ab}\otimes\ket{\phi_{ab}}\,. (1)

The 3636 states |ϕa​b⟩\ket{\phi_{ab}}, for one officer each, are listed in Table 1. The 1212 shaded cells are classical officers: a single basis state with coefficient 2/72=1/6\sqrt{2}/\sqrt{72}=1/6. The other 2424 are entangled officers, each a superposition of two basis states with coefficients ±1/72\pm 1/\sqrt{72}. The support of |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} thus has 12+2⋅24=6012+2\cdot 24=60 basis states |x⟩=|x1​x2​x3​x4⟩\ket{x}=\ket{x_1x_2x_3x_4}, where xj∈{0,…,5}x_{j}\in\{0,\dots,5\} is the index of party jj. With ψx=⟨x|ψ⟩\psi_{x}=\innerproduct{x}{\psi} we write

P={x:ψx=1/6},E={x:ψx=±1/72}P=\{x:\psi_{x}=1/6\},\qquad E=\{x:\psi_{x}=\pm 1/\sqrt{72}\}

for the 1212 basis states of the classical officers (PP) and the 4848 of the entangled ones (EE). For x∈Px\in P all four indices xjx_{j} lie in {0,3,4,5}\{0,3,4,5\} and exactly one of them is 00, e.g. |0344⟩\ket{0344}. For x∈Ex\in E exactly two of them lie in {1,2}\{1,2\}, e.g. |0012⟩\ket{0012}.

Proposition 1.

|ψ⟩\ket{\psi} is an AME(4,6)(4,6) state: the reshaped matrix U(i​j),(k​l)=6​ψi​j​k​lU_{(ij),(kl)}=6\psi_{ijkl} is a real orthogonal 2-unitary matrix of order 3636.

Proof.

We first show that UU is orthogonal, i.e. that the bipartition 12|3412|34 is maximally entangled: ρ12=U​UT/36=𝕀/36\rho_{12}=UU^{T}/36=\mathbb{I}/36. The row (a,b)(a,b) of UU is the officer |ϕa​b⟩/2\ket{\phi_{ab}}/\sqrt{2} of Table 1, written in the basis |x3​x4⟩\ket{x_3x_4} of parties 3,43,4. A classical officer gives a row with one entry 11, an entangled officer a row with two entries ±1/2\pm 1/\sqrt{2}. Every ket |x3​x4⟩\ket{x_3x_4} appears either in exactly one cell, or in exactly two cells that contain the same two kets. The rows of two such cells are therefore supported on the same two columns, which no other row uses, and after permuting rows and columns UU is a direct sum of 1212 blocks (1)(1) and 1212 blocks 12​(s1s2s3s4)\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}s_{1}&s_{2}\\ s_{3}&s_{4}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr) with si=±1s_{i}=\pm 1. For example, (a,b)=(0,0)(a,b)=(0,0) and (5,5)(5,5) give 12​(−1111)\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}-1&1\\ 1&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr). The two officers of a pair are orthogonal, s1​s3+s2​s4=0s_{1}s_{3}+s_{2}s_{4}=0, so every block, and hence UU, is orthogonal.

The same argument applies to URU^{R} and UΓU^{\Gamma}, the reshapings along 13|2413|24 and 14|2314|23, whose rows collect the basis states |x⟩\ket{x} with given indices (x1,x3)(x_{1},x_{3}) or (x1,x4)(x_{1},x_{4}). Each of them again has 1212 rows with one entry 11 and 2424 rows with two entries ±1/2\pm 1/\sqrt{2}, paired on the same two columns with orthogonal signs, so both are direct sums of 1212 blocks (1)(1) and 1212 orthogonal 2×22\times 2 blocks, whose block lists are part of the exact check in Ref. [23]. Hence also ρ13=ρ14=𝕀/36\rho_{13}=\rho_{14}=\mathbb{I}/36, and the complementary pairs follow because |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} is pure. So UU is 2-unitary and |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} is AME. ∎

All one- and two-party marginals have also been verified in exact arithmetic over ℚ⁡(2)\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}) [23]. Fig. 1 shows the three reshapings. In the golden state all 3636 officers are entangled [11]. The classical officers also make |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} as close to a product state as an AME(4,6)(4,6) state can be: for every product state |v⟩=|v1​v2​v3​v4⟩\ket{v}=\ket{v_1v_2v_3v_4}, |⟨v|ψ⟩|2≤⟨v1​v2|ρ12|v1​v2⟩=1/36|\innerproduct{v}{\psi}|^{2}\leq\langle v_{1}v_{2}|\rho_{12}|v_{1}v_{2}\rangle=1/36, so the overlap |⟨v|ψ⟩||\innerproduct{v}{\psi}| is at most 1/61/6, with equality at the 1212 states of PP.

III Symmetry and linearization

The state was obtained as a byproduct of a search for AME states in eigenspaces of local symmetries u⊗4u^{\otimes 4}, u=V​D​V†u=VDV^{\dagger}, with VV Haar random and DD diagonal of finite order. Two necessary conditions restrict DD and the eigenvalue λ\lambda. First, if u⊗4​|Φ⟩=λ​|Φ⟩u^{\otimes 4}\ket{\Phi}=\lambda\ket{\Phi}, the reshaping of |Φ⟩\ket{\Phi} along a cut A|AcA|A^{c} connects the μ\mu-eigenspace of u⊗|A|u^{\otimes|A|} only with the λ​μ¯\lambda\bar{\mu}-eigenspace of u⊗|Ac|u^{\otimes|A^{c}|}. For |A|=2|A|=2 the reshaping is proportional to a unitary, so these eigenspaces must have equal dimensions for every μ\mu, and for |A|=1|A|=1 the second must be at least as large. Second, in the eigenbasis of uu the populations |Φx|2|\Phi_{x}|^{2} must form a probability distribution on the basis states of the eigenspace with uniform two-party marginals (these are the diagonals of ρj​k=𝕀/36\rho_{jk}=\mathbb{I}/36), which is formulated as a linear feasibility problem. In particular, with complex unit ii, take V=𝕀V=\mathbb{I} and u=D=diag⁡(ik0,…,ik5)u=D=\mathrm{diag}(i^{k_{0}},\dots,i^{k_{5}}) with k=(1,2,2,3,3,3)k=(1,2,2,3,3,3). The −1-1 eigenspace of u⊗4u^{\otimes 4} is spanned by the 360360 basis states |x1​x2​x3​x4⟩\ket{x_1x_2x_3x_4} with kx1+⋯+kx4≡2(mod4)k_{x_{1}}+\dots+k_{x_{4}}\equiv 2\pmod{4}, and a random-start optimization in it finds AME states within a few restarts. Most of them have a 1010-dimensional space of first-order deformations modulo local unitaries (Sec. IV), the others a 33-dimensional one.11 1 A first-order deformation of an AME state |Φ⟩\ket{\Phi} is a vector |δ​Φ⟩\ket{\delta\Phi} such that the two-party marginals of |Φ⟩+t​|δ​Φ⟩\ket{\Phi}+t\ket{\delta\Phi} remain 𝕀/36\mathbb{I}/36 to first order in tt. For four parties it suffices to check ρ12\rho_{12}, ρ13\rho_{13} and ρ14\rho_{14}. These vectors form a real vector space. It always contains the tangent space of the local-unitary orbit, spanned by the vectors i⁡(H1⊗𝕀⊗𝕀⊗𝕀+⋯+𝕀⊗𝕀⊗𝕀⊗H4)​|Φ⟩i(H_{1}\otimes\mathbb{I}\otimes\mathbb{I}\otimes\mathbb{I}+\dots+\mathbb{I}\otimes\mathbb{I}\otimes\mathbb{I}\otimes H_{4})\ket{\Phi} with Hermitian HjH_{j}, and the dimension of the quotient is invariant under local unitaries. It is an upper bound on the number of parameters, modulo local unitaries, of any family of AME states through |Φ⟩\ket{\Phi}, with equality where the rank of the linearized conditions is locally constant. Local unitaries that commute with uu, namely U⁡(1)×U⁡(2)×U⁡(3)U(1)\times U(2)\times U(3) acting on the basis states |0⟩\ket{0}; |1⟩,|2⟩\ket{1},\ket{2}; and |3⟩,|4⟩,|5⟩\ket{3},\ket{4},\ket{5} of each party, preserve the eigenspace. Minimizing a smoothed ℓ1\ell_{1} norm of the coefficients over such changes of local basis can bring a solution with a 1010-dimensional deformation space to exactly 7272 non-zero coefficients. A subsequent Gauss–Newton optimization on that support makes it AME to machine precision [23]. These 7272 basis states form an orthogonal array of strength 22 and index 22 [25]. They consist of the 6060 basis states E∪PE\cup P of the support of |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} and 1212 further ones, which we call P′P^{\prime} (listed in Eq. (6)). As for PP, all four indices of each x∈P′x\in P^{\prime} lie in {0,3,4,5}\{0,3,4,5\} and exactly one of them is 00. Altogether, the 7272 basis states lie in the −1-1 eigenspace (∑jkxj≡2(mod4)\sum_{j}k_{x_{j}}\equiv 2\pmod{4} for each), so every state supported on them, including |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} and both families of Sec. IV, is a −1-1 eigenvector of u⊗4u^{\otimes 4}. Modulo an overall phase on each party, the diagonal local unitaries that act on this support as a scalar form the group ℤ2×ℤ2×ℤ4\mathbb{Z}_{2}\times\mathbb{Z}_{2}\times\mathbb{Z}_{4}, in which u⊗4u^{\otimes 4} has order 44.

An irredundant orthogonal array of index 11 gives an AME state as the uniform superposition of its rows [26]. With index 22 the phases must also cancel. In each of the three reshapings, the rows and the columns are labeled by the indices of two complementary pairs of parties, so strength 22 and index 22 mean that every row and every column has exactly two non-zero entries. Moreover, two rows that share a column share both of their columns, so after permuting rows and columns each reshaping is a direct sum of 1818 full 2×22\times 2 blocks [23]: the 1212 blocks of EE (the EE-blocks) from the proof of Proposition 1, and six mixed blocks with two states of PP on one diagonal and two of P′P^{\prime} on the other. Over the three reshapings this gives 3636 EE-blocks and 1818 mixed blocks. A block-diagonal matrix is unitary if and only if each of its blocks is, and for a 2×22\times 2 block this amounts to linear equations in the squared moduli and a single linear congruence in the phases: on such a support the AME conditions linearize. On the support E∪PE\cup P of |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} the six mixed blocks split into 1212 blocks of size 1×11\times 1, and the proof of Proposition 1 is this argument. Allowing both kinds of blocks gives the following lemma.

Lemma 1.

Let |Φ⟩=∑x∈SΦx​|x⟩\ket{\Phi}=\sum_{x\in S}\Phi_{x}\ket{x} with Φx=sx/72​ei​φx\Phi_{x}=\sqrt{s_{x}/72}\,e^{i\varphi_{x}}, where sx>0s_{x}>0 and φx∈ℝ\varphi_{x}\in\mathbb{R}. In each of the three reshapings UU, URU^{R}, UΓU^{\Gamma} of 6​|Φ⟩6\ket{\Phi}, along 12|3412|34, 13|2413|24 and 14|2314|23, the basis state |x⟩\ket{x} lies in the row labeled by its indices for the first pair of parties and in the column labeled by those for the second. For x∈Sx\in S in row rr and column cc we write sr​c=sxs_{rc}=s_{x} and φr​c=φx\varphi_{rc}=\varphi_{x}. Then |Φ⟩\ket{\Phi} is AME if and only if sx=2s_{x}=2 on every 1×11\times 1 block and every 2×22\times 2 block, with rows r,r′r,r^{\prime} and columns c,c′c,c^{\prime}, satisfies

sr​c=sr′​c′,sr​c′=sr′​c,sr​c+sr​c′=2,φr​c−φr​c′−φr′​c+φr′​c′≡π(mod2​π).\begin{gathered}s_{rc}=s_{r^{\prime}c^{\prime}},\quad s_{rc^{\prime}}=s_{r^{\prime}c},\quad s_{rc}+s_{rc^{\prime}}=2,\\ \varphi_{rc}-\varphi_{rc^{\prime}}-\varphi_{r^{\prime}c}+\varphi_{r^{\prime}c^{\prime}}\equiv\pi\pmod{2\pi}.\end{gathered} (2)

In particular, if these moduli equations have a solution with all sx>0s_{x}>0, a real AME state with support SS exists if and only if the equations tr​c+tr​c′+tr′​c+tr′​c′=1t_{rc}+t_{rc^{\prime}}+t_{r^{\prime}c}+t_{r^{\prime}c^{\prime}}=1, one for each 2×22\times 2 block, have a solution t∈𝔽2St\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{S}.

Proof.

The reduced state of parties 1,21,2 is ρ12=U​U†/36\rho_{12}=UU^{\dagger}/36, and that of parties 3,43,4 is ρ34=U†​U¯/36\rho_{34}=\overline{U^{\dagger}U}/36, and URU^{R} and UΓU^{\Gamma} give ρ13,ρ24\rho_{13},\rho_{24} and ρ14,ρ23\rho_{14},\rho_{23} in the same way. Hence |Φ⟩\ket{\Phi} is AME, i.e. all six two-party reductions equal 𝕀/36\mathbb{I}/36 (which includes ⟨Φ|Φ⟩=1\innerproduct{\Phi}{\Phi}=1), if and only if UU, URU^{R} and UΓU^{\Gamma} are unitary.

Fix one reshaping UU and its blocks. The entry of UU in row rr and column cc is sr​c/2​ei​φr​c\sqrt{s_{rc}/2}\,e^{i\varphi_{rc}} if the basis state there lies in SS, and 00 otherwise. Since the RkR_{k} and the CkC_{k} partition the rows and the columns and all entries of SS lie in the blocks Rk×CkR_{k}\times C_{k}, ordering the rows as R1,…,RmR_{1},\dots,R_{m} and the columns as C1,…,CmC_{1},\dots,C_{m} makes UU block diagonal, with diagonal blocks BkB_{k} the submatrices on Rk×CkR_{k}\times C_{k}. So UU is unitary if and only if every BkB_{k} is. A 1×11\times 1 block is unitary if and only if sx/2=1s_{x}/2=1. A 2×22\times 2 block BB with rows r,r′r,r^{\prime} and columns c,c′c,c^{\prime} is unitary if and only if its rows are orthonormal:

sr​c+sr​c′=sr′​c+sr′​c′=2,Br​c​B¯r′​c+Br​c′​B¯r′​c′=0.s_{rc}+s_{rc^{\prime}}=s_{r^{\prime}c}+s_{r^{\prime}c^{\prime}}=2,\qquad B_{rc}\bar{B}_{r^{\prime}c}+B_{rc^{\prime}}\bar{B}_{r^{\prime}c^{\prime}}=0.

Then B†​B=𝕀B^{\dagger}B=\mathbb{I} as well, so also sr​c+sr′​c=sr​c′+sr′​c′=2s_{rc}+s_{r^{\prime}c}=s_{rc^{\prime}}+s_{r^{\prime}c^{\prime}}=2. These four norm equations are equivalent to the three moduli equations in (2). Under them, the two terms of the orthogonality condition have the same modulus sr​c​sr​c′/2>0\sqrt{s_{rc}s_{rc^{\prime}}}/2>0, so their sum vanishes if and only if their phases φr​c−φr′​c\varphi_{rc}-\varphi_{r^{\prime}c} and φr​c′−φr′​c′\varphi_{rc^{\prime}}-\varphi_{r^{\prime}c^{\prime}} differ by π\pi modulo 2​π2\pi, which is the congruence. Conversely, the moduli equations and the congruence give orthonormal rows. So BB is unitary if and only if Eq. (2) holds. Exchanging rr with r′r^{\prime}, or cc with c′c^{\prime}, gives an equivalent system, so the labeling within a block does not matter. Collecting the conditions of all blocks of the three reshapings proves the first claim.

The moduli equations involve only ss and the congruences only φ\varphi, so any positive solution ss and any solution φ\varphi together give an AME state with support SS, and every such state arises in this way. It is real if and only if all φx∈{0,π}\varphi_{x}\in\{0,\pi\}. Writing φx=π​tx\varphi_{x}=\pi t_{x} with tx∈{0,1}t_{x}\in\{0,1\}, the congruence becomes tr​c−tr​c′−tr′​c+tr′​c′≡1(mod2)t_{rc}-t_{rc^{\prime}}-t_{r^{\prime}c}+t_{r^{\prime}c^{\prime}}\equiv 1\pmod{2}, which is the stated equation over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2}. ∎

IV Two families through the real state

We now describe, up to diagonal local unitaries, all AME states with support exactly E∪P∪P′E\cup P\cup P^{\prime}, E∪PE\cup P or E∪P′E\cup P^{\prime}. Let εx=±1\varepsilon_{x}=\pm 1 be the sign of ψx\psi_{x} for x∈Ex\in E. For δ∈[−1,1]\delta\in[-1,1] and phases αx\alpha_{x} (x∈Px\in P) and βx\beta_{x} (x∈P′x\in P^{\prime}) let

|Ψδ​(α,β)⟩=172[∑x∈Eεx|x⟩+1+δ∑x∈Pei​αx|x⟩+1−δ∑x∈P′ei​βx|x⟩].\ket{\Psi_\delta(\alpha,\beta)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{72}}\Big[\sum_{x\in E}\varepsilon_{x}\ket{x}\\ +\sqrt{1+\delta}\sum_{x\in P}e^{i\alpha_{x}}\ket{x}+\sqrt{1-\delta}\sum_{x\in P^{\prime}}e^{i\beta_{x}}\ket{x}\Big]. (3)

At δ=1\delta=1 the coefficients on P′P^{\prime} vanish and we write |Ψ1​(α)⟩\ket{\Psi_1(\alpha)}, since the phases β\beta play no role. At δ=−1\delta=-1 those on PP vanish, and we write |Ψ−1​(β)⟩\ket{\Psi_{-1}(\beta)}. A number in place of α\alpha or β\beta means that all phases on PP, or all phases on P′P^{\prime}, have that value. Thus, the real state in Eq. (1) is |ψ⟩=|Ψ1​(0)⟩\ket{\psi}=\ket{\Psi_1(0)}, while the other end with all phases zero is a different real AME state,

|ψ−⟩=|Ψ−1​(0)⟩=172​∑x∈Eεx​|x⟩+16​∑x∈P′|x⟩,\ket{\psi_-}=\ket{\Psi_{-1}(0)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{72}}\sum_{x\in E}\varepsilon_{x}\ket{x}+\frac{1}{6}\sum_{x\in P^{\prime}}\ket{x}, (4)

with the 1212 coefficients 1/61/6 on P′P^{\prime} instead of PP. No local unitary and permutation of the parties maps |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} to |ψ−⟩\ket{\psi_-} (Theorem 1), and no permutation of the parties and of the basis states of each party maps the support E∪PE\cup P onto E∪P′E\cup P^{\prime}. Each of the 1818 mixed blocks has two states x,y∈Px,y\in P on one diagonal and two states x′,y′∈P′x^{\prime},y^{\prime}\in P^{\prime} on the other. For |δ|<1|\delta|<1 the moduli of Eq. (3) satisfy the moduli equations of Lemma 1 on every block, and the EE-blocks carry the coefficients of |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} which satisfy their respective phase congruences. The only remaining AME conditions are therefore the phase congruences (2) of the mixed blocks, which read

αx+αy≡βx′+βy′+π(mod2​π).\alpha_{x}+\alpha_{y}\equiv\beta_{x^{\prime}}+\beta_{y^{\prime}}+\pi\pmod{2\pi}. (5)

P2\displaystyle P_{2} ={0455,3034,4540,5303},\displaystyle=\{0455,3034,4540,5303\},
P3\displaystyle P_{3} ={0533,3350,4404,5045},\displaystyle=\{0533,3350,4404,5045\},
P1′\displaystyle P^{\prime}_{1} ={0353,3530,4044,5405},\displaystyle=\{0353,3530,4044,5405\},
P2′\displaystyle P^{\prime}_{2} ={0434,3055,4503,5340},\displaystyle=\{0434,3055,4503,5340\},
P3′\displaystyle P^{\prime}_{3} ={0545,3304,4450,5033}.\displaystyle=\{0545,3304,4450,5033\}.

The mixed blocks join the quartets in a regular way: for all kk and ll, exactly two of them contain states of PkP_{k} and Pl′P^{\prime}_{l}, and their pairs split PkP_{k} into two pairs p,p¯p,\bar{p} and Pl′P^{\prime}_{l} into two pairs q,q¯q,\bar{q}, where partner pairs have the same first indices [23]. With α⁡(p)\alpha(p) the sum of α\alpha over pp, Eq. (5) for these two blocks reads

α⁡(p)≡β⁡(q)+π,α⁡(p¯)≡β⁡(q¯)+π.\alpha(p)\equiv\beta(q)+\pi,\qquad\alpha(\bar{p})\equiv\beta(\bar{q})+\pi. (7)

We call the AME states with support exactly E∪PE\cup P or E∪P′E\cup P^{\prime} the two faces, ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} and ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime}. Eq. (3) covers both faces at δ=±1\delta=\pm 1, but a face is more than the set of limits of the states with |δ|<1|\delta|<1: by Proposition 2(c), the AME states with support E∪P∪P′E\cup P\cup P^{\prime} reach each face only along a 99-dimensional subtorus.

Proposition 2.

(a) Up to diagonal local unitaries, the AME states with support exactly E∪P∪P′E\cup P\cup P^{\prime} are the states |Ψδ​(α,β)⟩\ket{\Psi_\delta(\alpha,\beta)} with |δ|<1|\delta|<1 that satisfy Eq. (5). They form two components ℱ72±∋|Ψδ(0,±π/2)⟩\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm}\ni\ket{\Psi_\delta(0,\pm\pi/2)}, exchanged by complex conjugation, with 1010 parameters each.
(b) Up to diagonal local unitaries, the AME states with support exactly E∪PE\cup P are the states |Ψ1​(α)⟩\ket{\Psi_1(\alpha)}, with 1111 parameters, and those with support exactly E∪P′E\cup P^{\prime} are the states |Ψ−1​(β)⟩\ket{\Psi_{-1}(\beta)}.
(c) |Ψ1​(α)⟩\ket{\Psi_1(\alpha)} is a limit of ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm} if and only if the sums of α\alpha over P1P_{1}, P2P_{2} and P3P_{3} agree modulo 2​π2\pi, and |Ψ−1​(β)⟩\ket{\Psi_{-1}(\beta)} is one if and only if the sums of β\beta over P1′P^{\prime}_{1}, P2′P^{\prime}_{2} and P3′P^{\prime}_{3} agree.
(d) No state of ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm} is real, even up to diagonal local unitaries.

Proof.

By Lemma 1, everything reduces to linear congruences in the phases. The ranks and invariant factors quoted below are computed exactly in Ref. [23]. We use two facts. (i) If a system of integer linear congruences in nn phases has rank ν\nu and invariant factors d1,…,dνd_{1},\dots,d_{\nu} (the non-zero entries of the Smith normal form of its matrix), its solutions, if any, form d1⋯dνd_{1}\cdots d_{\nu} disjoint (n−ν)(n-\nu)-dimensional tori. (ii) In each reshaping, a diagonal local unitary adds to φx\varphi_{x} a function of the row of xx plus a function of its column, which cancels in every congruence (2).

To tell the two components apart we use

ω=∑x∈P′,x1≠0φx−∑x∈P,x1≠0φx.\omega=\sum_{x\in P^{\prime},\,x_{1}\neq 0}\varphi_{x}-\sum_{x\in P,\,x_{1}\neq 0}\varphi_{x}.

The nine mixed blocks without a state of first index 00 contain each of these 1818 states exactly twice, so adding their congruences in the form (5) gives 2​ω≡π2\omega\equiv\pi: every AME state with support E∪P∪P′E\cup P\cup P^{\prime} has ω≡±π/2\omega\equiv\pm\pi/2. Diagonal local unitaries form a connected group that maps such states to such states, so they cannot change this discrete value, while complex conjugation reverses it.

(a) The moduli equations of the EE-blocks have rank 4848, so s=1s=1 on EE. On a mixed block they give sx=sys_{x}=s_{y}, sx′=sy′s_{x^{\prime}}=s_{y^{\prime}} and sx+sx′=2s_{x}+s_{x^{\prime}}=2. Every pair within a quartet lies in a mixed block, so ss is constant on each quartet, and, as noted before Eq. (7), every PkP_{k} shares a mixed block with every Pl′P^{\prime}_{l}, so s⁡(Pk)+s⁡(Pl′)=2s(P_{k})+s(P^{\prime}_{l})=2. Hence s=1+δs=1+\delta on PP and 1−δ1-\delta on P′P^{\prime}, with |δ|<1|\delta|<1 as s>0s>0. The 3636 congruences of the EE-blocks have rank 2828 in 4848 phases and invariant factors 11, so by (i) their solutions form one 2020-dimensional torus. By (ii) it contains the phases of |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} shifted by any diagonal local unitary, which also form a 2020-dimensional torus, so the two coincide. Hence a diagonal local unitary brings every AME state with this support to some |Ψδ​(α,β)⟩\ket{\Psi_\delta(\alpha,\beta)}, and such a state is AME if and only if Eq. (5) holds. This system has rank 1414 in 2424 phases and invariant factors 1,…,1,21,\dots,1,2, so by (i) its solutions form two disjoint 1010-dimensional tori. At (α,β)=(0,±π/2)(\alpha,\beta)=(0,\pm\pi/2), ω=±9π/2≡±π/2\omega=\pm 9\pi/2\equiv\pm\pi/2, so ω\omega tells the two tori apart. Together with δ\delta they give ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm}, on which ω≡±π/2\omega\equiv\pm\pi/2. Complex conjugation, (α,β)↦(−α,−β)(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto(-\alpha,-\beta), exchanges them, and no diagonal local unitary does. A diagonal local unitary that maps a state of the family to another must fix the coefficients on EE, and on P∪P′P\cup P^{\prime} it then acts by a common phase, possibly combined with the sign change of P3∪P′P_{3}\cup P^{\prime}. The common phase removes one of the 1010 phase dimensions, leaving 99 parameters besides δ\delta.

(b) On E∪PE\cup P the 1×11\times 1 blocks give s=2s=2 on PP and no phase condition, so the states are |Ψ1​(α)⟩\ket{\Psi_1(\alpha)} for all α\alpha, and the common phase leaves 1111 parameters. The same holds on E∪P′E\cup P^{\prime}.

(c) Let AkA_{k} and BlB_{l} be the sums of α\alpha over PkP_{k} and of β\beta over Pl′P^{\prime}_{l}. Adding the two congruences (7) gives Ak≡BlA_{k}\equiv B_{l}, so A1≡A2≡A3A_{1}\equiv A_{2}\equiv A_{3} on ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm}, and also on its limits, since |Ψδn​(αn,βn)⟩→|Ψ1​(α)⟩\ket{\Psi_{\delta_n}(\alpha_n,\beta_n)}\to\ket{\Psi_1(\alpha)} forces αn→α\alpha_{n}\to\alpha. Conversely, let A1≡A2≡A3A_{1}\equiv A_{2}\equiv A_{3} and Pl′={w,x,y,z}P^{\prime}_{l}=\{w,x,y,z\}. Each of its six pairs lies in one mixed block, so Eq. (5) prescribes the six pair sums σw​x≡βw+βx\sigma_{wx}\equiv\beta_{w}+\beta_{x}, and so on. By Eq. (7), the sums of complementary pairs, σw​x+σy​z\sigma_{wx}+\sigma_{yz}, σw​y+σx​z\sigma_{wy}+\sigma_{xz} and σw​z+σx​y\sigma_{wz}+\sigma_{xy}, are A1A_{1}, A2A_{2}, A3A_{3} in some order, hence equal. Therefore the solutions on Pl′P^{\prime}_{l} are exactly 2​βw≡σw​x+σw​y−σx​y2\beta_{w}\equiv\sigma_{wx}+\sigma_{wy}-\sigma_{xy} and βx≡σw​x−βw\beta_{x}\equiv\sigma_{wx}-\beta_{w}, βy≡σw​y−βw\beta_{y}\equiv\sigma_{wy}-\beta_{w}, βz≡σw​z−βw\beta_{z}\equiv\sigma_{wz}-\beta_{w}: two solutions, differing by π\pi on all of Pl′P^{\prime}_{l}, and eight in total. Adding π\pi on one quartet changes ω\omega by 3​π3\pi, so four of the eight lie in each component, and for each of them |Ψδ​(α,β)⟩→|Ψ1​(α)⟩\ket{\Psi_\delta(\alpha,\beta)}\to\ket{\Psi_1(\alpha)} as δ→1\delta\to 1. At δ=−1\delta=-1 the same holds with α\alpha and β\beta exchanged.

(d) If D​|Φ⟩D\ket{\Phi} were real for some |Φ⟩\ket{\Phi} in ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm} and a diagonal local unitary DD, it would have ω∈{0,π}\omega\in\{0,\pi\}. But it is AME with support E∪P∪P′E\cup P\cup P^{\prime}, so ω≡±π/2\omega\equiv\pm\pi/2. ∎

Branches through the real state. At α=0\alpha=0 all pair sums in the proof of (c) are σ≡π\sigma\equiv\pi, so β\beta is constant on each quartet Pl′P^{\prime}_{l} with 2​β≡π2\beta\equiv\pi, i.e. β=ηl​π/2\beta=\eta_{l}\pi/2 with ηl=±1\eta_{l}=\pm 1. The eight straight lines δ↦|Ψδ​(0,β)⟩\delta\mapsto\ket{\Psi_\delta(0,\beta)} are the branches through |ψ⟩=|Ψ1​(0)⟩\ket{\psi}=\ket{\Psi_1(0)}. Since ω=3​(η1+η2+η3)​π/2≡η1​η2​η3​π/2\omega=3(\eta_{1}+\eta_{2}+\eta_{3})\pi/2\equiv\eta_{1}\eta_{2}\eta_{3}\pi/2, four lie in ℱ72+\mathcal{F}_{72}^{+} and four in ℱ72−\mathcal{F}_{72}^{-}. Along a branch only the moduli change: as δ\delta decreases from 11 to −1-1, the coefficients on PP shrink from 1/61/6 to 00 and those on P′P^{\prime} grow from 00 to 1/61/6. At δ=−1\delta=-1 a branch ends at |Ψ−1​(β)⟩\ket{\Psi_{-1}(\beta)} on the opposite face. A common phase on P′P^{\prime}, which a diagonal local unitary applies without changing the coefficients on EE, makes this state real, and for constant β\beta it becomes |ψ−⟩\ket{\psi_-}. Up to diagonal local unitaries, the eight branches thus end at four real states, each reached by one branch from each component: |ψ−⟩\ket{\psi_-} and the three states obtained from it by negating the coefficients on P1′P^{\prime}_{1}, P2′P^{\prime}_{2} or P3′P^{\prime}_{3} (classes 99, 99, 1010, 99 of Theorem 1).

Uniform states. Halfway along a branch, at δ=0\delta=0, all 7272 coefficients have modulus 1/721/\sqrt{72}. For constant β=±π/2\beta=\pm\pi/2 they are εx\varepsilon_{x}, 11 and ±i\pm i times 1/721/\sqrt{72} on EE, PP and P′P^{\prime}. In every reshaping W=2​UW=\sqrt{2}\,U then has two entries from {±1,±i}\{\pm 1,\pm i\} in each row and column and W​W†=2​𝕀WW^{\dagger}=2\,\mathbb{I}: a 2-unitary complex weighing matrix (Fig. 2). These uniform states are new: the AME(4,6)(4,6) states reported earlier have at least 112112 non-zero coefficients, and the real states of Refs. [20, 22] have 6060 and 9696 (Sec. VI). Other uniform states of ℱ72+\mathcal{F}_{72}^{+} are almost real: up to a diagonal local unitary, ℱ72+\mathcal{F}_{72}^{+} contains a uniform state with coefficients ±1/72\pm 1/\sqrt{72} except for ±i/72\pm i/\sqrt{72} on the four states of P1′P^{\prime}_{1}, and a path of AME states in ℱ72+\mathcal{F}_{72}^{+} joins it to |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} (Fig. 3) [23]. Four imaginary coefficients are the minimum. If all coefficients of an AME state with support E∪P∪P′E\cup P\cup P^{\prime} lie in {±1,±i}/72\{\pm 1,\pm i\}/\sqrt{72}, then by Eq. (2) every block contains an even number of imaginary coefficients, while ω≡±π/2\omega\equiv\pm\pi/2 requires an odd number among the 1818 states of P∪P′P\cup P^{\prime} with x1≠0x_{1}\neq 0. The smallest sets with both properties are the six quartets [23].

The first-order deformations of an AME state, modulo the tangent space of its local-unitary orbit, form a local-unitary invariant, in the spirit of the defect of a unitary matrix [27]. Their dimension is 1010 for a generic member of ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm}, 1111 for a generic face state, and 1414 at |ψ⟩\ket{\psi}: 1111 directions along the face and 33 spanned by the eight branches (numerical ranks, with gaps of 10−1510^{-15} against 10−210^{-2}). The real state is thus a singular point of the AME conditions, where the 1111-dimensional face and both 1010-dimensional components meet (Fig. 3).

V Classification of the real states

Where the real states lie. None of the real states lies in ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm} (Proposition 2(d)), so they all lie on the two faces. Up to diagonal local unitaries, ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} is the 1111-torus of the phases α\alpha modulo a common phase and the sign change of P3P_{3}, which a diagonal local unitary with entries ±1\pm 1 performs without changing the coefficients on EE. Its origin is |ψ⟩\ket{\psi}. By Lemma 1, a face state is real up to diagonal local unitaries if and only if its phases are 00 or π\pi up to a diagonal local unitary, i.e. if and only if it is a point of order at most two of this torus. The real states of ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} are therefore exactly its 211=20482^{11}=2048 points of order at most two: 10241024 with all αx∈{0,π}\alpha_{x}\in\{0,\pi\}, and 10241024 with αx=±π/2\alpha_{x}=\pm\pi/2 on P3P_{3} and αx∈{0,π}\alpha_{x}\in\{0,\pi\} on P1∪P2P_{1}\cup P_{2}. On ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime}, with origin |ψ−⟩\ket{\psi_-}, the phases β\beta are determined modulo a common phase alone, and its 20482048 real states are those with all βx∈{0,π}\beta_{x}\in\{0,\pi\}. The closures of ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm} meet ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} only in the 99-torus 𝒞\mathcal{C} on which the quartet sums of α\alpha agree (Proposition 2(c)), and ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime} only in the corresponding 99-torus 𝒞′\mathcal{C}^{\prime}. The 29=5122^{9}=512 points of order at most two of each are the real states that are limits of ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm}. The other 30723072 real states lie only on the faces. The eight straight branches through a real state of 𝒞\mathcal{C} end at real states of 𝒞′\mathcal{C}^{\prime} only for the 128128 states of class 11 below, the class of |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} (at states of classes 99 and 1010), and for the other 384384 they end at non-real states [23].

Equivalently, a real state of ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} or ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime} is given by signs that solve the 3636 congruences of the EE-blocks over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2}: on each face there are 2322^{32} such sign patterns, and modulo diagonal local unitaries they give the 20482048 real states. Negating a coefficient 1/61/6 keeps a state AME, since these are 1×11\times 1 blocks. On each face, the permutations of the parties and of the basis states |0⟩,…,|5⟩\ket{0},\dots,\ket{5} of each party that map the support onto itself, and each officer (one or two basis states) onto an officer, form a group of order 192192, with 1616 orbits on the real states of ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} (88 of size 6464, 88 of size 192192) and 2424 on those of ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime} (44 of size 3232, 2020 of size 9696).

Theorem 1.

The 40964096 real AME(4,6)(4,6) states with support E∪PE\cup P or E∪P′E\cup P^{\prime} fall into exactly 2020 classes under local unitaries and permutations of the parties: 88 on ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} and 1212 on ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime}. Their representatives are listed in Table 2.

Proof.

At most 2020. States in one orbit are related by monomial local unitaries and party permutations. On each face, orbits are further joined by the real local orthogonal map H12⊗4H_{12}^{\otimes 4}, a 2×22\times 2 Hadamard rotation of the basis states |1⟩,|2⟩\ket{1},\ket{2} of every party, followed by a monomial map. This leaves 88 classes on ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} and 1212 on ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime} [23].
At least 2020. Local-unitary invariants have been used to separate AME states and their phase families [28, 29]. We use the spectrum of a Jacobian. Let JJ be the real Jacobian of the map Φ↦(ρA)|A|=2\Phi\mapsto(\rho_{A})_{|A|=2} to all six two-party marginals, and n⁡(t)n(t) the number of eigenvalues of 72​JT​J72J^{T}J below tt. A local unitary acts orthogonally on the state and on each marginal, and a party permutation permutes the marginals, so the spectrum of JT​JJ^{T}J, and hence n⁡(t)n(t), is invariant under both. The pairs (n⁡(149/8),n⁡(3/2))\bigl(n(149/8),n(3/2)\bigr) of the 2020 representatives are pairwise different (Table 2). To certify them, note that 72​JT​J72J^{T}J has entries in ℤ⁡[2]\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}] and splits into blocks of size at most 160160. For each block GG we form X=VT​(G−t​𝕀)​VX=V^{T}(G-t\mathbb{I})V in interval (ball) arithmetic [30], with VV the numerical eigenvectors of GG, and check that every Gershgorin interval of XX excludes 00. By Sylvester’s law of inertia, the number of negative intervals is then the number of eigenvalues of GG below tt. ∎

Simpler invariants do not separate the classes: the power traces Tr​(JT​J)k\mathrm{Tr}(J^{T}J)^{k}, k≤8k\leq 8, are equal on classes 33–88 (numerical). The real states are isolated: modulo local orthogonal maps, no continuous family of real AME states passes through any of them. Most orbits have no real first-order deformation. For the remaining six (two on ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60}, four on ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime}), the two real first-order deformations are obstructed at second order (numerical) [23]. Within the families of Sec. IV the real states are therefore isolated points of complex continua.

The deformation dimensions also separate our states from the known solutions: 1414 and 1111 for the real classes and 1010 for ℱ72±\mathcal{F}_{72}^{\pm}, against 44 for the golden state of Ref. [11] and 33 for the 2-unitary Hadamard matrix H⁡(0)H(0) of Ref. [13]. None of our states is locally equivalent to those (numerical ranks, with the same gaps as above).

VI Discussion

The real states have 6060 non-zero coefficients. Until the announcements of Refs. [20, 21, 22] the sparsest reported AME(4,6)(4,6) state was the golden state with 112112 [11, 12], whose representation of numerically minimized Rényi-2 decomposition entropy has 144144 [31]. Of the real states announced in parallel, that of Ref. [22] has 9696 and that of Ref. [20] also 6060. The argument of Sec. II also bounds the support of any AME(4,6)(4,6) state from below. A coefficient of modulus 1/61/6 exhausts the norm of its row and column in every reshaping, so the classical officers form a code of length 44 and minimum distance 33 over six symbols. Such a code has at most 3434 codewords [32]: 3636 would be a pair of orthogonal Latin squares of order six, and 3535 complete uniquely to 3636. Every other row needs at least two entries, so the support is at least 72−t≥3872-t\geq 38, where tt is the number of classical officers. Conversely, a state with s<72s<72 non-zero coefficients has at least 72−s72-s classical officers. All 3636 officers can be entangled only from support 7272 on, as in the uniform states of Sec. IV, and the 1212 classical officers of our 6060-term states are the minimum for their support. Whether the gap between 3838 and 6060 can be closed is open.

Other real solutions. Bruzda’s real state [20] is locally equivalent to |ψ⟩\ket{\psi}. Its variant with one coefficient negated [22] is |ψ⟩\ket{\psi} with the classical officer 04550455 negated, the representative of class 77, and the one-parameter phase family of Ref. [22] is a curve in ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60}. The 96-term real state of Ref. [22], invariant under a simultaneous cyclic shift of all four parties, is of a different kind. The degree-8 invariant KK of Ref. [22], evaluated on the tensor 6​Φi​j​k​l6\Phi_{ijkl}, the entries of the 2-unitary of a state |Φ⟩\ket{\Phi}, is 108108 for it, while it is 7272 on classes 11–22, 4040 on classes 33–88 and at most 00 on classes 99–2020, so that state is not equivalent to any of our real states. (KK takes only 1010 distinct values on our 2020 classes.) Its deformation dimension is 33, while every state of our families has at least 1010, so it lies outside both families. It also has no classical officer in any local basis: its overlap with every product state is below 0.98/60.98/6, so by the argument above each of its local representatives has at least 7272 non-zero coefficients (both numerical). The statements about the states of Refs. [20, 22] themselves were checked with the tools of Ref. [23] but are not among its scripts, which cover our states and the values of KK on them. Real coefficients alone therefore do not produce classical officers. In our states they come from the faces ℱ60\mathcal{F}_{60} and ℱ60′\mathcal{F}_{60}^{\prime}.

Further questions remain. Real AME(4,6)(4,6) states outside these families exist [22]. Whether other real states have classical officers is open. Do our real states admit a form with all amplitudes of modulus 1/361/36, i.e. a real-equivalent 2-unitary Hadamard matrix? Such a form would have to keep the 1212 product states of maximal overlap 1/61/6. The eigenspace of u⊗4u^{\otimes 4} also contains AME states outside the families: about one in eight search hits lies on a 33-parameter family of complex AME states with 348348 of the 360360 coefficients non-zero and deformation dimension 33, which we could not bring to a sparse or real form (numerical). Whether it is related to the Hadamard family of Ref. [13] or to the real state of Ref. [22] is open. Both H⁡(0)H(0) and that state also have deformation dimension 33. Finally, a real 2-unitary of order 3636 is a real perfect tensor: a real dual-unitary gate, and a building block of holographic codes with real amplitudes [3, 5].
